# Human and Articulated Avatars

Also called: Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction, Animatable 3D Gaussian Splatting

## Overview
This family of methods extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to reconstruct animatable human and articulated avatars from multi-view or monocular video inputs. It solves the problem of generating dynamic, high-fidelity 3D representations that can be rendered in novel poses and expressions, addressing the limitations of static reconstruction and the computational cost of traditional neural radiance fields. It differs from static [3D Gaussian Splatting Rendering (Software)](2805-3d-gaussian-splatting-rendering-software.md) by introducing deformation fields or parametric bindings to drive Gaussian positions and attributes over time, and from [Gaussian Splatting](../gaussian-splatting.md) by explicitly modeling articulated motion rather than static geometry.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core objective of mapping a canonical 3D Gaussian representation to a deformed state driven by pose or expression parameters. The general pipeline involves:
1.  **Canonical Initialization:** Initializing 3D Gaussians in a reference (canonical) pose or space.
2.  **Deformation Mechanism:** Defining a mapping function that transforms canonical Gaussian centers and potentially their attributes (opacity, spherical harmonics) to a target pose. This mapping is typically learned via optimization or a neural network.
3.  **Differentiable Rendering:** Rendering the deformed Gaussians using standard differentiable splatting to compute photometric loss against input images.
4.  **Optimization:** Updating Gaussian parameters and deformation model parameters to minimize rendering error.

The specific implementation of the deformation mechanism varies significantly, ranging from explicit mesh binding to implicit motion fields and cage deformations.

## Subtopics

### [GaussianHead](8051-gaussianhead.md)
GaussianHead is a method for animatable head reconstruction that uses a tri-plane representation and motion fields to simulate geometrically changing heads in continuous movements. It is designed to render rich textures, including skin and hair. It differs from [GaussianAvatars](8208-gaussian-avatars.md) by relying on implicit tri-plane/motion field representations rather than binding Gaussians to an explicit parametric mesh, and from [HeadGas](8210-headgas.md) by not using latent features weighted by 3DMM expression vectors. See [GaussianHead](8051-gaussianhead.md) for implementation details.

### [GART](8093-gart.md)
GART is a method that extends the human to more articulated models (e.g., animals) based on the 3DGS representation. It builds on [Human and Articulated Avatars](8209-human-and-articulated-avatars.md) by generalizing the 3D Gaussian Splatting framework beyond human subjects to other articulated entities. See [GART](8093-gart.md) for implementation details.

### [D3GA](8094-d3ga.md)
D3GA is a method for reconstructing animatable full-body human avatars from multi-view videos by combining drivable 3D Gaussians with tetrahedral cage deformation. It addresses the challenge of modeling dynamic human geometry and appearance, serving as a foundational approach in the lineage of Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction [Parent](8209-human-and-articulated-avatars.md). Unlike sibling methods that rely on linear blend skinning [GART](8093-gart.md) or specialized head-only representations [GaussianHead](8051-gaussianhead.md), D3GA utilizes tetrahedral cages to provide explicit geometry and appearance modeling for the full body. See [D3GA](8094-d3ga.md) for implementation details.

### 3D Gaussian Splatting for Human101
Human101 pushes the speed of high-fidelity dynamic human creation to 100 seconds using a fixed-perspective camera [S1][S2, unofficial].

### SplattingAvatar / GoMAvatar
SplattingAvatar and GoMAvatar embed Gaussians onto a canonical human body mesh [S1][S2, unofficial]. The position of a Gaussian is determined by the barycenter and displacement along the normal direction [S1][S2, unofficial].

### HeadGas
HeadGas attributes the 3DGS with a base of latent features that are weighted by the expression vector from 3DMMs [S2, unofficial]. This allows reconstruction in real-time of animatable heads [S2, unofficial].

### 3DPSHR
3DPSHR combines hand geometry priors (MANO) with 3DGS, to provide the first real-time hand reconstruction [S2, unofficial].

### MonoGaussianAvatar
MonoGaussianAvatar applies 3DGS to dynamic head reconstruction using canonical space modeling and deformation prediction [S2, unofficial].

### MANUS
MANUS explores the interaction between hands and objects using 3DGS [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The reconstruction of dynamic human avatars has traditionally relied on parametric models (SMPL, FLAME) combined with neural radiance fields (NeRF) or explicit mesh tracking. The advent of 3D Gaussian Splatting provided a faster, rasterization-based alternative for static scenes. Early adaptations for dynamic humans, such as GaussianAvatar, incorporated optimizable tensors and dynamic appearance networks to capture dynamics [S1]. Human101 further optimized the training speed for dynamic human creation [S1][S2, unofficial]. Subsequent works explored various deformation strategies: mesh-embedded Gaussians (SplattingAvatar, GoMAvatar) [S1][S2, unofficial], implicit motion fields (GaussianHead) [S1][S2, unofficial], and cage-based deformations (D3GA) [S1][S2, unofficial]. Head-specific reconstruction has seen specialized approaches like HeadGas using 3DMM-weighted latent features [S2, unofficial] and GaussianHead using tri-planes [S1][S2, unofficial]. The family has expanded to include hands (3DPSHR, MANUS) [S2, unofficial] and non-human articulated figures (GART) [S1][S2, unofficial].
